summary.locked_approach: Preprocess each AFM frame (row-level + square pixels), then use targeted reciprocal-space mapping (fourier_reflection_map) to detect and quantify the periodic lattice/ordered-adsorbate reflection and its spatial coherence, and compare presence/spacing/coherence between 2 mM and 10 mM to characterize how ordering changes with KCl concentration.

detailed_analysis:
This series aims to characterize how the surface structure/adsorbate pattern on mica evolves between 2 mM and 10 mM KCl using AFM height maps. Two frames were analyzed with a rigorous, artifact-aware pipeline (per-row median leveling escalated to polynomial subtraction, streak-removal verification, square-pixel resampling, fourier_reflection_map with strict streak-axis artifact rejection and null/SNR/coherence gating). Both frames passed quality verification (scores 0.79 and 0.87, mean 0.83), and streak removal was fully successful in the 2 mM frame (streak_std reduced from ~1341 to ~4e-12 after escalation to polynomial leveling).

The critical finding is that the intended comparative analysis is essentially UNRESOLVED, because only the 2 mM frame produced extractable quantitative features. The 10 mM entry has empty extracted_features and quality_metrics, so no spacing, domain fraction, SNR, or reflection-count values are available for it. Consequently the 'trend' between concentrations is degenerate: every feature is reported as a single point with no regression possible.

For the 2 mM frame, the pipeline detected 28 candidate reflections and a nominal periodicity of ~0.392 nm at a frequency of ~0.498 cyc/px, with a high sigma-resolvability (7.65). However, this reflection was NOT confirmed as real ordered-adsorbate/lattice content: reflection_present is False, the domain SNR (14.5) is substantially LOWER than the bulk SNR (34.7), so spot_snr_domain_gt_bulk is False and reflection_confirmed_domain_gt_bulk is False. The domain fraction is very small (~0.025, i.e. ~2.5% of the field). A frequency of ~0.498 cyc/px is essentially at the Nyquist limit (0.5 cyc/px), which is a classic signature of a pixel-grid / single-pixel-alternation artifact rather than genuine surface periodicity. Combined with the fallback pixel calibration (100 nm FOV assumption, 0.195 nm/px), the '0.392 nm' spacing is an artifact of the Nyquist frequency times an assumed pixel size, not a physically meaningful lattice constant. The gating logic correctly declined to confirm this as a real reflection.

Taken together, the data support a conservative conclusion: at 2 mM KCl, no resolvable, spatially-coherent ordered-adsorbate lattice reflection is confirmed above bulk background, and at 10 mM no quantitative features were extractable at all. The comparative objective (how structure changes from 2 to 10 mM) therefore cannot be answered from the present dataset; the most defensible statement is that neither frame provides confirmed evidence of an ordered adsorbate superlattice under these imaging/calibration conditions.

scientific_claims.claim: At 2 mM KCl on mica, no ordered-adsorbate/lattice reflection is confirmed above bulk background: the leading Fourier candidate (~0.498 cyc/px, i.e. at the Nyquist limit) has lower domain SNR (14.5) than bulk SNR (34.7) and occupies only ~2.5% of the field, failing the domain>bulk confirmation gate.
scientific_claims.scientific_impact: Establishes a rigorous null result and prevents over-interpretation of near-Nyquist Fourier peaks as genuine atomic/adsorbate lattices, which is a common pitfall in high-resolution AFM of electrolyte-mica interfaces.
scientific_claims.has_anyone_question: Has anyone rigorously distinguished genuine ordered-adsorbate lattice reflections from Nyquist-limit pixel-grid artifacts in AFM height maps of the KCl–mica interface using domain-vs-bulk SNR gating?

individual_results.name: (hard) fmica 2mM KCl
individual_results.analysis_type: AFM per-row leveling + square-pixel resample + fourier_reflection_map reciprocal-space mapping of ordered-adsorbate/lattice reflection (KCl ordering).

individual_results.name: (hard) fmica 10mM KCl
individual_results.analysis_type: Comparative AFM (KCl concentration): per-frame row-flatten + streak-removal verification/escalation (chained from median subtraction), square-pixel resample, fourier_reflection_map reciprocal-space mapping with strict streak-axis artifact rejection and null/SNR/coherence gating; differential presence/spacing/coherence compared between concentrations.

flagged_images_analysis.summary: No images were formally flagged by the QC pipeline; both frames were approved. However, the 10 mM frame is effectively a silent failure: it passed quality verification (score 0.87) yet returned empty extracted_features and quality_metrics, so it contributes no usable data to the comparative objective.
possible_causes: The 10 mM analysis may have found 'no resolvable order' (a legitimate finding per the pipeline) but failed to populate the feature dictionary with the null values.
A pipeline serialization/reporting bug: features were computed but not written to the summary dict.
Genuine absence of any detectable reflection at 10 mM, causing the reflection-mapping step to return empty rather than explicit nulls.
The 10 mM image may have had stronger streaking, tip artifacts, or drift that caused the reflection-mapping stage to abort after leveling.
recommended_followup: Re-run the 10 mM analysis and explicitly force reporting of null-result features (spacing=None, domain_fraction, SNRs) rather than an empty dict.
Inspect the 10 mM leveled image and its Fourier map directly to confirm whether the empty result is a true null or a reporting failure.
Acquire the true FOV/scale metadata to replace the fallback 100 nm assumption, since pixel calibration directly controls whether the near-Nyquist peak maps to a plausible spacing.
Collect replicate frames at each concentration to distinguish stochastic imaging quality from concentration-dependent structure.
flagged_images_analysis.scientific_significance: The 'flagged' status is administrative rather than physical: the missing 10 mM data is a data-completeness problem, not evidence of interesting physics. The genuinely interesting observation is the conservative null at 2 mM.

refit_analysis.summary: No images were adaptively re-analyzed with alternative pipelines. However, within the standard pipeline, the 2 mM frame required escalation from median row-subtraction to per-row polynomial (1st-2nd order) subtraction to fully remove streaks (streak_std_after ~4e-12).

pipeline_changes.interpretation: The escalation indicates residual low-order row bowing/tilt beyond a simple constant offset — consistent with scanner bow, thermal drift, or gradual baseline curvature in the fast-scan direction. This is an instrumental/leveling issue, not a structural change of the mica surface.

refit_analysis.scientific_implications: The need for polynomial leveling reflects instrumental baseline characteristics rather than sample physics. No structural transition or morphology change can be inferred from the leveling escalation. The near-Nyquist candidate reflection surviving into detection underscores the importance of the artifact-rejection gates, which correctly prevented an aggressive-leveling residual from being mistaken for real ordering.

trend_analysis.approach: Single control variable (KCl concentration: 2 mM, 10 mM), so I use the standard trend dashboard with feature values on the y-axis vs. KCl concentration on the x-axis. Because only two concentration points exist, I connect them with straight lines (a 2-point 'trend' is degenerate for regression confidence, but I still fit and report a linear slope per feature to quantify direction/magnitude of change, framing the objective: how the ordered-adsorbate/lattice reflection signature evolves from 2 mM to 10 mM). The 10 mM entry has empty extracted_features/quality_metrics, so the script robustly handles missing values by plotting only available points and annotating missing data. Key panels track reflection presence/confirmation, reflection spacing, domain fraction & SNR (domain vs bulk), and streak-removal/leveling quality metrics. Regression slopes are computed and printed where >=2 numeric points exist.
trend_analysis.flagged_handling: No images were flagged; the script still contains logic to overlay red X markers on any flagged index if present. Missing-feature entries (e.g., empty 10 mM dict) are annotated as 'no data' rather than plotted as zero.

reflection_present/confirmed.interpretation: 2 mM frame is unconfirmed (False); 10 mM has no data. No confirmed ordered structure at either point that can be quantified.

reflection_spacing_nm.interpretation: Only a single 2 mM value (0.392 nm) exists, and it corresponds to a near-Nyquist frequency under fallback calibration, so it is likely an artifact rather than a physical lattice spacing. No trend determinable.

domain_fraction.interpretation: Only 2 mM measured (~0.025), indicating any ordered content occupies a negligible fraction of the field. No comparison possible with 10 mM.

spot_snr_domain vs spot_snr_bulk.interpretation: At 2 mM, domain SNR (14.5) < bulk SNR (34.7), meaning the candidate reflection is weaker than background — evidence against real ordered content. No 10 mM data.

reflection_sigma_resolvability.interpretation: High value (7.65) at 2 mM reflects a sharp Fourier peak, but sharpness alone (especially near Nyquist) does not establish physical validity. No 10 mM data.

n_reflections_detected.interpretation: 28 candidate reflections at 2 mM prior to gating; most are rejected by artifact/SNR gates. No 10 mM data.

caveats: The comparative objective cannot be answered: only 1 of 2 frames yielded quantitative features (the 10 mM frame is empty), so no true concentration trend can be established — all 'trends' are single-point and degenerate. Pixel calibration relied on a fallback 100 nm FOV assumption, so the reported 0.392 nm spacing is not metrologically reliable; its frequency (~0.498 cyc/px) sits at the Nyquist limit, a strong indicator of a pixel-grid artifact rather than a real lattice. The single detected candidate at 2 mM failed the domain>bulk SNR gate (14.5 < 34.7) and occupies only ~2.5% of the field, so no confirmed ordered structure exists even at 2 mM. With only two concentrations and no replicates, statistical confidence is minimal. Conclusions should be limited to (a) a conservative null at 2 mM and (b) a data-completeness failure at 10 mM requiring re-analysis with explicit null reporting and true scale metadata before any concentration-dependence claim is made.

locked_analysis_config.analysis_approach: Preprocess each AFM frame (row-level + square pixels), then use targeted reciprocal-space mapping (fourier_reflection_map) to detect and quantify the periodic lattice/ordered-adsorbate reflection and its spatial coherence, and compare presence/spacing/coherence between 2 mM and 10 mM to characterize how ordering changes with KCl concentration.
locked_analysis_config.processing_pipeline: Per-row median subtraction for row alignment (median is robust to blobs) -> VERIFY streak removal: extract line profiles perpendicular to fast-scan over featureless regions; if residual row-to-row offset or streaks remain, ESCALATE to per-row 1st-2nd order polynomial subtraction and re-verify -> resample to square pixels using metadata FOV (512x512 no-op; 256x512 upsample slow axis to 512x512 assuming square FOV; record nm/px via resolve_pixel_size_nm; fall back to cyc/px with explicit caveat if calibration unavailable), preserving true aspect ratio -> fourier_reflection_map on the leveled square-pixel image -> ARTIFACT REJECTION: reject any detected reflection whose orientation is aligned with the residual streak axis (i.e. a horizontal-streak-induced vertical-frequency ridge) unless it independently passes the null-gate AND spot_snr_domain > spot_snr_bulk AND the domain map corresponds to real image content (not edge/streak bands) -> compare spacing, sigma, domain_fraction, spot_snr_domain vs spot_snr_bulk between 2 mM and 10 mM; report 'no resolvable order' as a legitimate finding for 10 mM if criteria are not met.
features_to_extract: primary lattice/adsorbate reflection spacing (nm if calibrated, else cyc/px)
reflection significance (sigma) / whether periodic order is resolvable at all
spot SNR in domain vs bulk (coherence of ordering)
orientation of any detected reflection relative to the fast-scan/streak axis (to distinguish real lattice from streak artifact)
qualitative change in ordering between 2 mM and 10 mM (including explicit 'order lost' if 10 mM has no resolvable reflection)
locked_analysis_config.quality_criteria: Preprocessing verified: horizontal streaks removed after row alignment, confirmed by a flat line profile across the fast-scan direction over featureless regions; if streaks persist (as is likely on the 10 mM frame), escalation to per-row polynomial is applied and re-verified before any FFT. Resampled image is 512x512 with recorded nm/px matching FOV/N when calibration exists (else pixel units flagged), with true aspect ratio preserved. Science verified via the tool's own fields: fourier_reflection_map returns periodic=True with at least one reflection above its significance floor AND spot_snr_domain > spot_snr_bulk for a claimed ordered frame; any reflection oriented along the residual-streak axis is treated as a suspected artifact and rejected unless it independently satisfies the null-gate and domain-map coherence checks. A reported 'no resolvable reflection' for the 10 mM frame is accepted and reported as a genuine loss-of-order finding, not forced. Any reported spacing is physically plausible for mica/adsorbate lattices (sub-nm, ~0.5 nm) when calibrated. Amplitude/domain maps must correspond to real image content, not streak bands, edges, noise, or NaN.
